title: Transfer: Copy a List with Random Pointers
oneLiner: Deep-copy a linked list where every node also has a pointer to any node in the list (or null). The map from Clone a Graph does the work again.
keyTakeaway: Whenever several references can reach the same object, a deep copy needs a map from each original object to its copy, keyed by the object itself, not its value. Build all the copies first, then wire every pointer by looking up the original target in the map.
explanation:
This follows Clone a Graph. Each node of a singly linked list has a value, a next pointer and a random pointer, which can point at any node in the list (an earlier one, a later one, the node itself) or be null. Return a deep copy: new nodes only, with next and random wired exactly like the original, and the original left untouched.

The tests describe the list as pairs [value, random index], with -1 meaning a null random pointer. The harness builds real nodes, calls your function on the head, and checks that no node in your copy is an original node, that every random pointer lands on a node of the copy, and that the original list was not changed. Values can repeat, so a map keyed by value will mix nodes up.

Copying next pointers alone is easy: walk and make a new node per old one. The random pointers are the problem. When you copy node 1 and its random points at node 4, the copy of node 4 may not exist yet, and when it does exist you need a way to find it from the original node 4. That is exactly the question the map answered in Clone a Graph: given an original node, where is its copy?

Two passes keep it simple. Pass 1 walks the list and creates the copy of every node, storing original to copy in a dictionary. Pass 2 walks again and, for each original n, sets copy(n).next to copy(n.next) and copy(n).random to copy(n.random), with null staying null. Every lookup succeeds because every copy was made in pass 1. That is O(n) time and O(n) extra space for the map. (A known O(1) space trick interleaves each copy right after its original, wires the random pointers through that layout, then splits the two lists apart. It is worth knowing, but the map version is the one to reach for first.)

The visualization copies the list [7, 13, 11, 10, 1] whose random pointers are null, 0, 4, 2 and 0. Each cell shows a node's value and where its random pointer goes.

Explain why the same idea works: before you move on, write two or three sentences on why the original to copy map from Clone a Graph is what this problem needs. Cover what the random pointers do to the shape of the list (is it still just a line?), which of the map's two jobs from Clone a Graph you still need here and which one the plain next walk already does for you, and why the key has to be the node object rather than its value.

recognitionSignals: "Deep copy" of a structure where one object can be reached through more than one reference.
A linked list with an extra pointer (random, child, sibling) that can point anywhere in the list.
gotchas: Key the map by node, not by value: two nodes with the value 3 are different nodes.
Look up random targets only after every copy exists (two passes), or create missing copies on demand when you first meet them.
Don't return or reuse an original node anywhere in the copy, including through a random pointer.
confusableWith: Graph Traversal + Hash Map: Clone a Graph uses the same map, but there it is also the visited set that stops a cycle from being copied forever. A list walked with next has no cycles, so here the map only finds copies.

complexity.note: Two walks of the list, each lookup O(1) on average. The map holds one entry per node. Interleaving each copy after its original avoids the map and gets O(1) extra space, not counting the copy itself.

referenceSolutions.python:
def copy_random_list(head):
    # Pass 1: one copy per original node, found again through the dict.
    copies = {}
    n = head
    while n is not None:
        copies[n] = Node(n.val)
        n = n.next

    # Pass 2: every copy exists now, so each pointer is one lookup.
    n = head
    while n is not None:
        copies[n].next = copies[n.next] if n.next is not None else None
        copies[n].random = copies[n.random] if n.random is not None else None
        n = n.next
    return copies[head] if head is not None else None
